name: OFFCUT: a community print exchange
project: A fictional community print studio is promoting a one-evening print exchange. The same visual treatment must work as a small poster and a social tile; only the 1000 px portrait poster is fixed for this comparison.
audience: Local adults who make things, art students, and people curious about printmaking but unfamiliar with studio jargon. The local information is in Polish.
medium: A 1000 px portrait event poster preview, later adapted to an A3 print and a social image. Judge the title both at full size and in a quarter-size view.
tone: Tactile, playful and confident, with enough character to feel like a small independent studio. Avoid precious luxury, wedding invitation, or corporate conference cues. Do not assume that distressed or handwritten lettering is the only route.
main_task: Make OFFCUT memorable, then let the viewer recover what the event is, its date, location and participation rule without searching.
language: The main title is the ASCII word OFFCUT. Polish supporting copy contains diacritics and must remain intact. A title face need not cover unused Polish letters if the supporting role uses a verified suitable face.
hierarchy: One dominant title; a short studio statement; clear date/time and place; a smaller instruction. The title and information must be judged together.
surroundings: Warm orange paper, near-black ink, one thin divider. Keep the supplied colors and copy. No illustrations, shadows, gradients or extra brand marks.
existing_baseline: The supplied neutral current typography is a control fixture, not a recommended direction. An expressive change is invited, but one family or retaining parts of the current system is acceptable if it serves the work.
design_freedom: Choose typography, title line break and role sizes. Title size 100–170 px; supporting text 24–38 px; caption 20–26 px. Keep width 1000 and padding 64. You may vary whitespace or leading, but keep information order and max height 1500. Prefer no more than two families.
acceptance: Title is fully visible at full and quarter-size, with no clipped ink or unresolved overlaps.
All Polish supporting text, including ł, ń, ó, ę and ż, renders from the chosen exact supporting face.
Date, place and participation instructions remain easy to locate beneath the expressive title.
If pairing two families, explain the relationship using the actual composition, not generic serif/sans labels.
Record whether character comes at the expense of information and revise if it does.
